about: The chaos suite's legs (C14 brief, amended 2026-10-20): each harness/cases/<case>.sh, variant and repeat is one leg of chaos.yml. The restart cases run 3 times and run-chaos.sh prints the worst outage. n is the brief's case number. `owed` (C14 fix round 3, item 4) names the docs/_INDEX.md Owed row behind each check a leg is known to fail (a row, or a list tried in order), so run-chaos.sh's table says which reds are explained; it never changes a verdict, and an owed red is as red as any other. A row is named for a failed check only when its `owed_signatures` filter (jq over that leg's verdict.json, its measures the evidence of the row's own cause) holds in that run (fix round 4, the re-review's I-3); else the check reads NOT OWED with the signature absent. A row leaves the map when its fix merges, and a red on its checks then reads NOT OWED: Owed 85 (a restarted container's CEF never starting; PR #54, main 263b08a), Owed 84 (a late sink's backlog; PR #57) and Owed 70 (a) (a fast GPU-death loop counted late; PR #55), all 2026-10-24, main 567cfcc. Owed 87 (the stall rule never beating rtmp2sink's own 5 s socket timeout) left it by a ruling, not a fix: the owner, 2026-10-24, "A", retired the rule, so the sink's error is the only stall detector and cases 5, 12 and 17 witness that path; a red on their checks reads NOT OWED. Owed 86 (case 6's clock under CPU starvation) left it by a ruling too: the owner, 2026-10-25, "A", made the clock trio (window_fps, pts_gaps, scheduled_changes_shown) measures in case 6 only, the starvation being induced below what performance-4x is sized for, with the viewer's quality on real CPU gated by the soak and the C15 cost legs; a red on case 6 reads NOT OWED. Cases 4, 5 and 12 each run twice, once per phase of the clear (no variant: a connect pending; `backoff`: after one failed; the re-review's I-5).
